name: Lightforge Iron
summary: In Menethil Harbor, Glorin Steelbrow seeks the lost cargo of an elven destroyer. The Flying Osprey carried rare Lightforge iron when it sank with the Third Fleet of Kul Tiras during the Second War.

sections.title: A Sacred Cargo
sections.body: The Flying Osprey sailed from Lordaeron with the Third Fleet of Kul Tiras. The elven destroyer carried a precious cargo of Lightforge iron and traveled beside the fleet for safety. But the Dragonmaw clan's enslaved red dragons swept down from the sky. They set the fleet ablaze, sending sailors and sanctified metal beneath the waves.

sections.title: Plundered by the Tides
sections.body: South of Menethil Harbor, the shattered Flying Osprey lies beneath the water. Its chest has been battered open and clawed through. Coastal murlocs scavenged the wreck and scattered the ingots, leaving little of the precious ore Glorin Steelbrow seeks.

faq.answer: The Flying Osprey was an elven destroyer sailing from Lordaeron during the Second War. It carried rare Lightforge iron alongside the Third Fleet of Kul Tiras for safety, until Dragonmaw's enslaved red dragons burned and sank the fleet.

Glorin Steelbrow is a dwarf stationed at Menethil Harbor in the Wetlands. He seeks historical salvage and valuable materials from the sunken ships along the coast, especially legendary metals like Lightforge iron.
Lightforge iron is a rare, sanctified metal used to forge consecrated arms and armor. Smiths and champions of the Holy Light value its purity and spiritual resilience.

faq.q: Why were the ships sunk in the Wetlands?
faq.answer: During the Second War, the Horde's Dragonmaw clan used the Demon Soul to enslave the Red Dragonflight. Dragonriders attacked Kul Tiras's Third Fleet off the Wetlands coast, burning the ships and sending them to the ocean floor.

faq.q: Why is the chest nearly empty?
faq.answer: Coastal murlocs clawed open the waterlogged chest aboard the Flying Osprey and plundered its cargo. Most of the ingots are gone, scattered along the marshy shore.

faq.q: Where is the wreckage of the Flying Osprey located?
faq.answer: The Flying Osprey lies among the coastal shoals just south of Menethil Harbor, along the western shore of the Wetlands. Its wreckage is split across the shallows near local murloc settlements.

angles.text: As a blacksmith, you can see why smiths revere Lightforge iron. They prize its powerful blessings and unmatched structural integrity.
As a paladin, you know weapons made from Lightforge iron are deeply attuned to the Holy Light. Recovering even one lost ingot carries spiritual weight.
As an Alliance member, you can see the sunken ships off Menethil Harbor as solemn memorials to the Second War. Sailors from Kul Tiras and Lordaeron fell to dragonfire there.
